ch20.d.N: Number of gas particles in the box
ch20.e.goal.S: Entropy $S = k\ln W$: the log of the number of microstates $W$ allowed by a macrostate (particles $n$ in the left half)
ch20.e.goal.irr: Statistical origin of irreversibility: the gas moves to the macrostate with the most microstates ($n \approx N/2$) and almost never comes back
ch20.e.obs.peak: $W(n)$ bars: largest at $n = N/2$; the highlighted bar is the current macrostate
ch20.e.obs.small: $N = 4$: all particles often gather in the left half again (probability $1/2^4 = 1/16$)
ch20.e.obs.large: $N = 1000$: probability $1/2^{1000} \approx 10^{-301}$, so the initial state never returns in practice; $n$ only fluctuates by about $\sqrt N/2$ around $N/2$
ch20.e.obs.S: $S(t)$: rises quickly, then fluctuates just below its maximum $S_\text{max}$
ch20.e.assume: Non-colliding particles (ideal gas), specular walls. The partition is removed at $t = 0$, with every particle in the left half
ch20.h.d.na: Number of oscillators in solid A; solid B has the rest ($N_\text{A} + N_\text{B} = 100$)
ch20.h.d.q: Total number of energy quanta $\varepsilon$ shared by the two solids
ch20.h.d.start: Solid that holds every quantum at the start (the other is at $T = 0$)
ch20.h.goal.flow: Heat flows in the direction that increases the total number of microstates $\Omega_\text{A}\Omega_\text{B}$, that is, from hot to cold
ch20.h.goal.T: Equilibrium: $S_\text{tot}$ is largest, so $\partial S_\text{A}/\partial E_\text{A} = \partial S_\text{B}/\partial E_\text{B}$; this defines temperature, $1/T = \partial S/\partial E$
ch20.h.obs.flow: Quanta hop at random both ways, but the net flow goes from A to B and $S_\text{tot}$ rises
ch20.h.obs.max: $S$-$q_\text{A}$ diagram: the current state (dot) climbs to the top of the $S_\text{tot}$ curve
ch20.h.obs.slope: At the top the tangents of $S_\text{A}$ and $S_\text{B}$ have equal and opposite slopes, so $kT_\text{A} = kT_\text{B}$
ch20.h.obs.size: $N_\text{A} = 30$, $N_\text{B} = 70$ (default): at equilibrium the energies are not equal ($q_\text{A} \approx 30$); the temperatures are
ch20.h.obs.fluct: After equilibrium $q_\text{A}$ keeps fluctuating, but $S_\text{tot}$ stays near its maximum
ch20.h.assume.model: Einstein solids: quantum oscillators of one frequency that exchange energy only in quanta $\varepsilon$. One random move: one oscillator passes one quantum to another (every microstate equally likely)
ch20.h.assume.T: Temperature from the large-$N$ form $kT/\varepsilon = 1/\ln(1 + N/q)$, with $q_\text{A}$ averaged over 1.5 s (a thermometer's response time); the readouts and the $kT/\varepsilon$ graph show this value
ch20.h.assume.arrow: $Q$ arrow: from the hotter to the colder solid by the displayed temperatures. Shown when they differ by more than 30 % of the larger, hidden below 15 %, at most one change per second; hidden at once if the order reverses
ch20.c.d.tc: Temperature of the cold reservoir that takes the waste heat (hot reservoir at 600 K)
ch20.c.goal.limit: Efficiency of a Carnot engine $e = 1 - T_\text{C}/T_\text{H}$: the upper limit for any engine working between two reservoirs
ch20.c.goal.ts: On a $T$-$S$ diagram the Carnot cycle is a rectangle: area under the path = heat, enclosed area = net work
ch20.c.obs.legs: A→B isothermal expansion (takes in $Q_\text{H}$), B→C adiabatic expansion, C→D isothermal compression (gives off $Q_\text{C}$), D→A adiabatic compression
ch20.c.obs.ratio: The two isotherms span the same entropy change, so $Q_\text{C}/Q_\text{H} = T_\text{C}/T_\text{H}$ and the gas has $\Delta S = 0$ over a cycle
ch20.c.obs.tc: Lowering $T_\text{C}$ raises the efficiency (200 K: 0.667, 400 K: 0.333)
ch20.c.obs.gas: Diatomic gas: the $p$-$V$ loop changes shape but the efficiency is the same
ch20.c.assume.ideal: Ideal gas, about 0.401 mol, A: 10 L, 600 K
ch20.c.assume: Quasi-static, reversible steps; reservoirs large enough to keep their temperatures; no friction
